los.text: Perform a clinical examination of the neck and thyroid gland.
los.html:
1Introduction, consent, sit the patient on a chair (so you can stand behind), glass of water.
2. HandsTremor (outstretched), sweating, palmar erythema, thyroid acropachy (Graves'), pulse (rate, AF).
3. Face and eyesExophthalmos, lid retraction, lid lag (follow a finger down), ophthalmoplegia (Graves' eye disease); dry hair, puffy face (hypothyroidism).
4. Neck inspectionSwelling, scars; ask to swallow (goitre and thyroid nodules rise) and stick out the tongue (thyroglossal cyst rises).
5. Palpate from behindBoth lobes and isthmus while swallowing; size, surface (smooth, multinodular, single nodule), tenderness; lymph nodes.
6Percuss the sternum (retrosternal extension), auscultate for a bruit (Graves').
7. ReflexesSlow-relaxing (hypothyroid), brisk (hyperthyroid); proximal myopathy (stand from a chair).
  • Finish: TFTs, ultrasound, antibodies.

los.text: Explain an endocrine condition to an older adult using clear and age-appropriate language.
los.html:
TechniqueExample (type 2 diabetes in a 78-year-old)
Check hearing, glasses, preferred paceSit at eye level, face them
Find out what they know"What have you heard about diabetes?"
Plain words, short chunks"Your body isn't handling sugar well"
Relate to their lifeDiet, activity, family support
Check understanding (teach-back)"Can you tell me what the tablet is for?"
Involve family/carers (with consent)
Written information in clear, large print
Safety-net and follow-upWhen to seek help

los.text: Perform a rapid A to E assessment of a patient presenting with sepsis, demonstrating the ability to identify key clinical signs, prioritise interventions, and make appropriate clinical decisions to manage the patient's condition.
los.html:
StageSepsis findingsAct
APatent?Airway support
BRR ≥22, low satsOxygen to target
CTachycardia, hypotension (SBP ≤100), prolonged CRT, mottled, low urine outputIV access, cultures, lactate, fluids
DNew confusion, glucoseTreat hypoglycaemia
ETemperature (>38 or <36), source (chest, urine, skin, abdomen, lines), non-blanching rashTreat source
  • Recognise: NEWS2 ≥5 (or 3 in one parameter) with suspected infection = think sepsis
    • red flag sepsis (NICE): systolic ≤90
    • HR ≥130
    • RR ≥25
    • new confusion
    • needs oxygen for sats ≥92%
    • non-blanching rash
    • mottled
    • no urine 18 h
    • lactate ≥2 → senior review and antibiotics within 1 hour.

los.text: Explain and demonstrate an understanding of the Sepsis Six pathway, including the key interventions and their role in the timely management of sepsis.
los.html:
Sepsis Six (within 1 hour)
Give 3Oxygen (target 94–98% / 88–92%)
IV antibiotics (broad spectrum, per guidelines)
IV fluids (500 mL crystalloid bolus, reassess; up to 30 mL/kg)
Take 3Blood cultures (before antibiotics, if no delay)
Lactate (and FBC, U&E, CRP)
Urine output (hourly; catheter if needed)
  • Also: senior review, find and control the source
    • escalate to critical care if lactate >4 or hypotension persists after fluids (septic shock).

los.text: Demonstrate the correct technique for conducting a clinical examination of the cervical spine, identifying relevant anatomical landmarks and interpreting key physical findings.
los.html:
StepDetail
LookPosture, head tilt, muscle spasm, scars, wasting
FeelSpinous processes, paraspinal muscles, tenderness
MoveFlexion (chin to chest), extension, lateral flexion (ear to shoulder), rotation (look over each shoulder)
NeurologicalUpper limb myotomes, dermatomes and reflexes; check for myelopathy (Hoffmann's, gait, lower limb UMN signs)
Special testsSpurling's (extension, rotation and axial load reproduces radicular arm pain)
  • Red flags: trauma, weight loss, fever, progressive neurological deficit, myelopathy, rheumatoid (atlantoaxial instability).
